r04-fuel-glutamine-his: L-Glutamine (watch Dr. Rhonda vid) is the main fuel for your enterocytes, and for your immune cells when they're activated. It doesn't have to go through the complicated digestive steps other nutrients do. Inside the mitochondria, it gets turned straight into alpha-ketoglutarate, or α-KG. The α-KG goes into the citric acid cycle, which is how the mitochondria make their energy. So that's why consuming pure glutamine gives energy to those cells faster than eating food. They then use their extra energy to repair the gut lining, and that keeps LPS from getting through.
r04-fuel-butyrate-his: The colonocytes lining your large intestine are fueled by short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate, while your small intestine runs on glutamine. Your gut bacteria make SCFAs when they ferment raw resistant starch, and you get SCFAs directly from your home-brewed SIBO yogurt too. Besides feeding the colonocytes, SCFAs lock down the barrier in your lower gut, preventing the dangerous escape of substances from gut to blood, which then turns down inflammatory signals that would be needed otherwise to contain the damage.
